title: free the same pointer twice, with the free count equal in both images
object: a, 24 bytes; b is allocated so the control has a second legitimate free
control: frees b instead of a the second time, so both images make exactly two st_free calls. The bug image leaves b to st_alloc_fini, which is a leak Valgrind is run with --leak-check=no to ignore.

asan.why: WHAT ASAN'S ANNOTATION INTERFACE CANNOT EXPRESS. Poison and unpoison describe ADDRESSABILITY; a double free is an error of OWNERSHIP, and there is no access to instrument. The arena's st_free only clears a liveness flag in its side table, so the second call finds the object dead and does nothing ASan can see. The free list pushes the block a second time, unpoisoning the link word before it writes it, so ASan sees nothing there either.

valgrind.why: THE ROW WHERE VALGRIND'S INTERFACE BEATS ASAN'S: VALGRIND_MEMPOOL_FREE models allocation identity, so freeing a block the pool does not currently hold is reported as an invalid free. Both annotated pools pass every st_free to it (the arena since B1.2), so both annotated arms win and the unannotated ones cannot.

hwasan.why: malloc's own metadata check. HWASan has no public custom-allocator interface, so the annotated columns are UNSUPPORTED, not MISSED (C3.4).

ubsan.why: -fsanitize=bounds needs a statically known array bound; a pointer out of an allocator has none. The row is kept so the report can say UBSan is not a heap tool rather than leaving it out.

lowfat.why: Bounds only; a free is not an access. to verify whether LowFat's runtime rejects it at the allocator level.

status: written, smoke-run on malloc, arena and freelist; server run pending (A5)
